A monsoon trough extends southeastward from Typhoon Dolphin to a
poorly-defined monsoon disturbance, newly designated Invest 98W, near
the far north Marianas. The monsoon trough then curves northeast 
towards Tropical Storm Chan-Hom (previously Invest 96W) to the 
distant northeast. An unsettled monsoon pattern dips south across the
CNMI. A strong, squall line-like feature produced an area of 
numerous to widespread showers and scattered thunderstorms west of 
coastal waters earlier today, then gradually stretched eastward 
across Rota this afternoon. Satellite trends indicated numerous 
locally heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms training across 
Rota, producing minor flooding late this afternoon and into the 
evening. Model guidance shows this feature shifting north, following 
a tilt in the monsoon trough. This is expected to bring numerous 
showers to Tinian and Saipan later this evening, capable of producing
occasional gusts to 35 mph, and trend down to scattered showers with
isolated thunderstorms after midnight. Several monsoon disturbance 
linger near the far northern Marianas, this upcoming week keeping a 
wetter pattern nearby, however, there may be some lulls in the active
weather pattern depending how convection organizes around these 
monsoon disturbances. Some uncertainty remains since this is tied to 
the actual location and intensity of the monsoon disturbances in the 
coming days.

Marine/Surf...
A Small Craft Advisory remains in effect through Sunday night. A High
Surf Advisory remains in effect along west and north facing reefs
through Monday afternoon and a high risk of rip currents continues
along west, north, and east facing reefs through Monday afternoon. 
Moderate to strong westerlies prevail across the Marianas over the 
weekend as another resurgence in the monsoon builds, likely to 
maintain moderate to strong winds through the middle of next week. 
Combined seas of 8 to 11 feet are expected over the next few days, 
remaining hazardous to small craft through at least early next week. 
Hazardous surf is expected to continue along west and north facing 
reefs of the Marianas through Monday, in addition to the high rip 
current risk along west, north, and east facing reefs. Rip current 
risk may drop to moderate along east reefs over the weekend as 
northwesterly and easterly swells decrease.

Tropical Systems...
The only system that's currently in Guam's AOR (Area of
Responsibility) is Invest 98W. This is a newly-formed Invest, dubbed
98W from JTWC (the Joint Typhoon Warning Center) near Maug island in
the far northern CNMI. The LLCC (Low- Level Circulation Center is 
only visible when viewing an in- house scatterometer data program 
that combined three different types of scatterometer data, but it's 
there. The LLCC is fairly close to 19N144E, but visible imager shows
a better cyclonic circulation that's slightly elevated closer to 
19.1N 143.4E. This circulation has formed in the saddle of a trough 
that enters Guam's AOR near Iwo To, stretches southeast to 98W in a 
saddle shape (bowing curved bottom), before turning northeast and 
connecting with newly- formed TD Chan-Hom (14W), which is located 
well north of Wake Island and out of Guam's AOR. Where 98W has 
formed, it's also at the tail- end of a ridge axis that stretches 
northward, and co-located in a col between the two more-developed 
tropical systems of Typhoon Dolphin (well outside of Guam's AOR near 
Okinawa), and Chan-Hom.

98W is in a favorable environment characterized by warm SSTs (Sea 
Surface Temperatures) and low wind shear. The ECENS is way more "hot 
and heavy" (faster/stronger) than the GEFS in the development of 98W,
but in general they show a developing tropical cyclone east of the 
Marianas and heading towards Wake Island in about 2 to 4 days.

Then, quickly moving in on its heels, are the remnants of TD Kujira 
(13W), which has has exited Luzon and looks to enter Guam's AOR in 24
hours. The visible imagery suggests the LLCC has been torn apart. 
However, similar to 98W, the ECENS is way more aggressive/faster in
redeveloping a LLCC with forming in 18-24 hours near the northern-
most CNMI. Meanwhile, the GEFS waits until it's exited the island
chain to the east, developing it more slowly as it heads towards Wake
Island.

Eastern Micronesia...
The light gentle winds and fair skies continue at Pohnpei and Kosrae
(although Kosrae had it's daily build-up near the mountains, while 
the coastal drive was more cloud free. At Majuro however, a sign of 
things to come is present there, as increased moistening and an 
embedded disturbance crossing the Date Line has lead to overcast 
skies. However, the cloudy (overcast) skies didn't prevent Majuro 
from topping out at 89 degrees, 2 degrees cooler than yesterday 
(we'll take it!).
